findings.fact: A combat character carries ordinary items as up to 224 full item-entity handles beginning at +0x1624; each item has an inventory position at +0x73c and 255 means unslotted.
findings.evidence: InventoryByClassname 0x10335950 iterates indices 0..223 and compares the pointed entity classname at +0x11c. Inventory removal 0x10335470 compacts the handle array and rewrites positions. Decoded tutorial saves show the same loose lockpick entity transition from owner -1/position 255 to player-owned/position 30.
findings.consequence: The remake inventory must preserve item identity, ownership and entity lifetime; a classname set is insufficient.

findings.fact: Character.HasItem searches ordinary slots case-insensitively and then searches logical records inside the carried item_g_keyring; Character.RemoveItem has the same fallback.
findings.evidence: PyHasItem 0x10198640 calls 0x10335950 then 0x10178470. KeyringFind 0x10407e10 searches count +0x920 in 0xc0-byte records at +0x914 with Q_strnicmp capped at 0x60. PyRemoveItem 0x10199240 falls through to 0x101784c0/0x10407e90.
findings.consequence: Keys are keyring membership records after collection but remain visible through the ordinary script predicate/removal surface.

findings.fact: Character.RemoveItem decrements m_iItemCount for a stack of at least two, but detaches and destroys a non-stackable item or the last stack member; no match still returns None.
findings.evidence: PyRemoveItem 0x10199240 calls the IsStackable virtual, reads +0x8d0, and selects decrement or Inventory_Remove 0x10335470 plus entity removal. Keyring removal is attempted only after ordinary lookup fails.
findings.consequence: Script removal is destructive and must not be conflated with player drop or the entity-valued Inventory_Remove input.

findings.fact: Character.AmmoCount is class-dependent: stackable items return +0x8d0, while non-stackable items return primary loaded-magazine count +0x74c; Character.GiveAmmo adds to stack count or the combat-character reserve pool for ammo type +0x744.
findings.evidence: PyAmmoCount 0x101989b0 and PyGiveAmmo 0x10198b30 select on IsStackable. The firearm return operand is +0x74c even though the path resolves its ammo type/reserve. GiveAmmo reaches the combat-character reserve-ammo virtual for non-stackable items.
findings.consequence: For firearms AmmoCount means clip, while GiveAmmo means reserve; the tutorial .38 dialogue depends on that asymmetry.

findings.fact: Character.HasWeaponEquipped compares the active handle at +0x19a4 against the supplied classname exactly and case-sensitively.
findings.evidence: PyHasWeaponEquipped 0x101984c0 resolves the active entity and performs an exact byte/string comparison rather than the case-insensitive inventory lookup.
findings.consequence: Owned and active are distinct predicates, and classname normalization must not change this retail edge.

findings.fact: item_container is a CBaseCombatCharacter inventory. equip0..equip11 spawn real entities; SpawnItemInContainer creates one; AddEntityToContainer moves unowned targetname matches; DeleteItems destroys all contents.
findings.evidence: ContainerSpawn 0x10209350, AddEntity 0x10208e50, SpawnItem 0x10208f30 and DeleteItems 0x10208fa0 use the common inventory add/remove paths. DeleteItems calls entity removal for each of 224 slots and clears slot, active and last handles.
findings.consequence: Containers and actors share ownership/stack transfer machinery; authored equip keys are spawn seeds, not a second contents format.

findings.fact: Container use opens exclusive loot mode through the barter service, and server CmdBarter authoritatively implements Take, Give, Buy and Sell with entity transfer or stack split/merge.
findings.evidence: ContainerUse 0x10208c90 tracks one user and selects showloot/hidebarter. CmdBarter 0x100da230 maps Take container-to-player, Give player-to-container, Buy vendor-to-player and Sell player-to-vendor; Take/Give fire OnItemRemove/OnItemInsert.
findings.consequence: The client UI requests transfers but never owns inventory mutation. The separate price formula remains economy scope.

findings.fact: trigger_inventory_check evaluates on accepted player StartTouch, searches ordinary slots and keyring case-insensitively, and fires OnPlayerHasItem without disabling itself.
findings.evidence: CTriggerInventory vtable 0x1048a134 slot 174 resolves to 0x10216d60. The body runs the base filter, requires the player component, performs both lookups and fires output +0x59c. No self-disable occurs.
findings.consequence: The predicate is entry-driven and player-only; a map output must author one-shot behavior.
